Keep the figure unchanged
Every position in each example row contains the same blue circle. Neither the shape, colour nor size changes.
The last row already contains two identical blue circles. Another identical blue circle completes it.
Add one nested outline
Moving right adds a smaller outline of the same shape inside the previous one. The outer shape and its colour stay unchanged.
The green triangle has one inner triangle in the middle position. Add one more, smaller inner triangle to obtain the answer.
Use the first shape as a cut-out
The black shape in the first position is removed from the centre of the coloured square in the second position. The hole is white.
The black square makes a square hole in the green square. Choose the green square with the white square opening.
Combine the upper and lower colours
The result takes its upper half from the first capsule and its lower half from the second capsule.
The first capsule is white and the second is blue, so the result is white above and blue below.
Rotate the coloured lobes
At each step, turn the whole four-lobed figure 90 degrees clockwise. Every red and blue lobe moves with the figure.
Turn the middle figure another quarter-turn clockwise. The two red lobes finish on the right and at the bottom; the top and left lobes are blue.
Round the corners progressively
The colour and general shape remain the same while the corners become more rounded at each step.
Continue rounding the corners of the brown rectangle. The answer is the brown capsule with fully rounded ends.
Continue the circle’s movement
Within each row the green circle moves the same distance in the same direction: upward, downward or horizontally. Its size stays fixed.
In the last row the circle moves left along the bottom of the square. One more equal step places it at the bottom left.
Turn the entire dot pattern
Rotate the square and all its dots 45 degrees counterclockwise at each step. The square becomes a diamond, then a square again.
Turn the middle green-and-black diamond another 45 degrees counterclockwise. Keep the green and black dots in their rotated positions.
Shorten each bar from the top
At every step, each vertical black bar loses one grid interval from its upper end. Its lower end stays on the bottom line. A bar disappears when its length reaches zero.
The middle picture has a one-interval middle bar and a two-interval right bar. The middle bar disappears, leaving a one-interval bar on the right.
Reflect across the black line
The middle line is a mirror axis. Reflect the coloured shape in that line rather than simply rotating it.
The last mirror line is vertical, so the yellow shape is flipped left to right. Its colour and size remain unchanged.
Overlay the shapes and use the first colour
Place both shapes on top of one another. Keep the combined silhouette and the visible outlines, but colour the result with the first shape’s colour.
Overlay the blue downward triangle and the yellow hexagon, then use blue for the combined figure. The triangle’s projecting tips remain visible around the hexagon.
Keep green in exactly one input
Compare corresponding areas of the two squares. An area is green if it is green in exactly one input. Green in both cancels to white; white in both stays white.
The first square is entirely green and the second has only a green bottom-left quarter. That shared quarter turns white; the other three quarters stay green.
Attach a copy at every corner
Put a copy of the small black symbol at each vertex of the large shape. The added copies take the large shape’s colour.
The large blue diamond has four corners. Add a blue downward triangle at each corner, following the same placement rule as the examples.
Add corresponding bar heights
For each of the three horizontal positions, add the black bar’s height in the first picture to its height in the second. Measure upwards from the common bottom line.
Neither input has a left bar. The two middle bars add to a full-height bar, while the right bars add to a shorter bar. The answer has just those middle and right bars.
Rotate and alternate colours
Turn the shape 45 degrees counterclockwise at each step. Its colour alternates, so the third picture returns to the first picture’s colour.
Turn the white middle shape another 45 degrees counterclockwise and restore the dark colour from the first picture. Choose the dark curved shape in that orientation.
Combine the black circles
A circle is black in the result whenever the matching circle is black in either input. It is white only when both inputs have a white circle there.
The first input contributes the bottom-right black circle; the second contributes the two top black circles. The centre and bottom-left circle stay white.
Expand into neighbouring cells
At each step, every blue cell remains blue and also colours its immediate neighbours above, below, left and right. Expansion stops at the grid boundary.
Apply the same one-cell expansion to the middle blue region. Newly reached side neighbours become blue; cells farther away remain in the grey-and-black checkerboard.
Cancel matching brown positions
Compare the two five-cell strips position by position. A cell is brown in the result if exactly one input is brown there. Matching brown cells cancel to blue.
Brown occurs in positions 2, 3, 4 and 5 in the first strip and in positions 2, 3 and 5 in the second. Only position 4 remains brown.
Remove the closest red dots
Find the smallest distance between any two red dots. Remove every red dot belonging to a pair at that distance. Recalculate the closest distance for the next step.
In the middle picture, the three lower red dots participate in the closest diagonal pairs. Removing them leaves only the red dot in the top row, fourth column.
Move the six colours around a cycle
Read down the left stack, then down the right stack. Shift every colour one position forward in that six-position cycle; the bottom-right colour wraps to the top left.
From the middle picture, the bottom-right brown circle wraps to the top left. The final stacks are brown/red/red on the left and black/brown/blue on the right.
Move white and black in opposite directions

White circles move one corner clockwise and black circles move one corner counterclockwise at each step. Grey means that a white and a black circle occupy the same corner; separate them before moving again.

The middle picture contains white circles at the two left corners and black circles at the two left corners and bottom right. Moving them gives white at top left, grey at top right, and black at both bottom corners.
Extend every horizontal stroke
At each step, extend each black horizontal stroke into the immediately neighbouring capsule on both sides. Existing strokes remain, and strokes stop at the outside edges.
Extend the strokes in the middle picture one more capsule left and right. Keep separate stroke heights distinct; the answer shows the resulting longer horizontal lines across the four capsules.
Grow the triangular lattice
Treat the drawing as a group of small triangles. At each step, add a small triangle just outside every exposed edge, keeping the existing triangles and their connecting lines.
Grow the middle green cluster by one more layer of neighbouring triangles. The answer keeps the same triangular grid and adds the triangles along its outside edges.
Remove the marked vertices
The brown dots identify vertices of the black polygon to remove. Connect the remaining vertices in their original order. Two remaining vertices produce a line segment.
Remove the top and left vertices marked by the brown dots. Only the two lower vertices remain, so the answer is the short horizontal line near the bottom right.
Toggle the dots at the outline’s corners
Match the black outline’s vertices to the 3-by-3 dot positions. At each vertex, remove an existing blue dot or add one if the position is empty. Other positions stay unchanged.
Toggle the four corner positions of the slanted outline. The result has blue dots at top left and top middle, middle middle and middle right, and all three bottom positions.
Remove the marked brick and its neighbours
First remove the red brick and every brick sharing an edge with it, then let unsupported bricks fall straight down. Repeat the same process with the yellow brick.
After the red removal, the remaining bricks form the middle staircase. Removing the yellow brick and its touching neighbours leaves the upper blue brick, which falls to the bottom.
Cycle the layers and apply the colour mask

Track the same three shapes. At each step the front shape goes to the back. For the final picture, keep the middle picture’s grey or black fills; its unfilled white shapes regain their colours from the first picture.
The grey hexagon comes to the front, the black horizontal capsule lies behind it, and the vertical capsule moves to the back. That white vertical capsule regains its original yellow colour.
Use each circle’s colour to find its motion

Track each circle relative to the circle immediately around it. White moves 90 degrees clockwise, black moves 90 degrees counterclockwise, and red stays in the same relative position. Blue does not move. Apply these movements to every nested level.

The black circle moves from above the blue circle to its left. Red stays to the right inside black. The larger white circle moves from above red to its right; the smallest white circle moves from below the larger white circle to its left.
Move colours along the connected routes

The black links specify the routes along which the colours move. Follow each loop clockwise, moving each colour to the next connected position. A two-position route swaps its colours; unconnected dots stay put.
Swap the two top colours. On the lower loop, the left-middle blue moves to the centre and the right-middle red moves to the bottom left. The unconnected bottom-right red stays unchanged.
Move each colour along its own path

Red moves down, green moves right and yellow moves left. Blue moves up and, where possible, one column left. White marks overlapping colours; separate those colours again when applying the next move. Colours moving beyond the grid disappear.
Separate the middle white cell into red and green. Red moves to bottom middle, green to middle right, blue reaches top left and yellow exits on the left. Those three coloured cells form the answer.
Move red and blue tips in opposite directions

At each step, every red tip moves one position counterclockwise and every blue tip moves two positions clockwise around the five-pointed star. White means that red and blue overlap; separate both colours before moving again.

In the middle picture, red is at the lower right and blue is at the upper right and upper left. The next move puts red and one blue together at the upper right, making it white. The other blue moves to the lower left.
Shift two copies in the sector’s directions

The two edges of the white sector indicate two movement directions. Make two copies of the red-dot pattern and shift one copy one grid step in each direction, wrapping at the edges. A position reached once is red; a position reached by both copies is blue.
The final sector points down-left and down-right. Shift a copy each way. Their overlap makes the entire top row and the centre blue; the single-copy positions remain red, as shown in the answer.
Remove crossing string segments

Overlay both drawings. Treat each straight piece between successive grid dots as a separate string segment. When a segment from one drawing crosses a segment from the other between dots, remove both segments. Segments meeting at a grid dot stay. Keep all uncut segments from both drawings.

Remove the diagonal segments cut between the grid dots. The remaining pieces form an upper fork with a vertical stem, two detached short diagonals near the top corners, and a lower fork with its own vertical stem.
Slide and sort the pieces by size

Push all pieces in the arrow’s direction. Smaller pieces pass larger pieces and reach the furthest available spaces first. Keep every piece’s height and vertical position. Pieces may share a column if they do not overlap vertically; equal-sized pieces keep their relative order.

The arrow points right. Fit the shortest pieces into the available spaces on the right, then the two-cell pieces, then the taller pieces to their left. Nothing moves up or down, and no piece changes size.
Move the dividers into free spaces
All black dividers simultaneously move one position to the right if the next position contains a yellow bead. A divider blocked by another divider waits. The right edge connects to the left edge.
Apply one simultaneous step to the middle sequence. The final order is divider, bead, divider, bead, divider, divider, bead.
Expand the colours and keep the largest group

Replace every coloured ball with four new balls of the same colour, one step above, below, left and right. Balls leaving the grid disappear. At each position, keep the colour with the largest number of arriving balls. If colours tie for the largest number, leave the position empty. Several arrivals of the same colour appear as one coloured marker.

Expanding the displayed middle picture leaves green at the top right and at row 2, column 3; red at row 2, column 1; and brown at row 2, column 2, row 3, column 3, and row 4, columns 2, 3 and 4. Those are exactly the colours and positions in the stored answer.

en.The black circle moves from above the bl: The black circle moves from above the blue circle to its left. Red stays to the right inside black. The larger white circle moves from above red to its right; the smallest white circle moves from below the larger white circle to its left.

en.Red moves down, green moves right and ye: Red moves down, green moves right and yellow moves left. Blue moves up and, where possible, one column left. White marks overlapping colours; separate those colours again when applying the next move. Colours moving beyond the grid disappear.

en.The final sector points down-left and do: The final sector points down-left and down-right. Shift a copy each way. Their overlap makes the entire top row and the centre blue; the single-copy positions remain red, as shown in the answer.
en.Overlay both drawings. Treat each straig: Overlay both drawings. Treat each straight piece between successive grid dots as a separate string segment. en.Remove the diagonal segments cut between: Remove the diagonal segments cut between the grid dots. The remaining pieces form an upper fork with a vertical stem, two detached short diagonals near the top corners, and a lower fork with its own vertical stem.

da.First remove the red brick and every bri: Fjern først den røde klods og alle klodser, der deler en kant med den. Lad klodser uden støtte falde lodret ned. Gentag med den gule klods.
da.After the red removal, the remaining bri: Efter første fjernelse danner klodserne trappen i midten. Når den gule klods og dens kantnaboer fjernes, bliver den øverste blå klods tilbage og falder til bunden.
da.Track the same three shapes. At each ste: De samme tre figurer følges gennem rækken. For hvert trin flytter den forreste figur bagerst. I sidste billede bevares gråt og sort fra midterbilledet, mens hvide figurer får deres oprindelige farve tilbage.
da.The grey hexagon comes to the front, the: Den grå sekskant kommer forrest med den sorte vandrette kapsel bagved. Den lodrette kapsel flytter bagerst og bliver gul igen.
da.Track each circle relative to the circle: Følg hver cirkel i forhold til cirklen umiddelbart udenom. Hvid flytter 90 grader med uret, sort 90 grader mod uret, og rød bevarer sin relative placering. Blå flytter ikke. Gør det på alle niveauer.
da.The black circle moves from above the bl: Sort flytter fra over den blå cirkel til venstre for den. Rød bliver til højre inde i sort. Den store hvide flytter fra over rød til højre for den; den mindste hvide flytter fra under den store hvide til venstre for den.
da.The black links specify the routes along: De sorte forbindelser viser farvernes ruter. Følg hver løkke med uret, og flyt hver farve til næste forbundne plads. To forbundne pladser bytter farve. Prikker uden forbindelse bliver stående.
da.Swap the two top colours. On the lower l: Byt de to øverste farver. I den nederste løkke flytter blå fra venstre side til midten, og rød fra højre side til nederst til venstre. Den uforbundne røde prik nederst til højre bevares.
da.Move each colour along its own path: Flyt hver farve ad sin egen rute
da.Red moves down, green moves right and ye: Rød flytter ned, grøn til højre og gul til venstre. Blå flytter op og, hvor det er muligt, én kolonne til venstre. Hvid viser overlappende farver, som adskilles før næste flytning. Farver uden for gitteret forsvinder.
da.Separate the middle white cell into red: Adskil den hvide midtercelle i rød og grøn. Rød flytter til nederste midte, grøn til midterste højre, blå til øverste venstre, og gul forlader gitteret mod venstre.
da.Move red and blue tips in opposite direc: Flyt røde og blå spidser hver sin vej
da.At each step, every red tip moves one po: For hvert trin flytter røde spidser én plads mod uret og blå to pladser med uret rundt om stjernen. Hvid betyder overlap af rød og blå; flyt begge farver hver for sig i næste trin.
da.In the middle picture, red is at the low: I midten er rød nederst til højre og blå øverst til højre og venstre. Næste trin samler rød og én blå øverst til højre, som bliver hvid. Den anden blå ender nederst til venstre.
da.Shift two copies in the sector’s directi: Forskyd to kopier i sektorens retninger
da.The two edges of the white sector indica: Den hvide sektors to kanter viser to bevægelsesretninger. Lav to kopier af det røde prikmønster, og forskyd én kopi ét gittertrin i hver retning. Fortsæt rundt ved kanterne. Én kopi giver rødt; overlap af begge giver blåt.
da.The final sector points down-left and do: Sidste sektor peger skråt ned mod venstre og højre. Forskyd en kopi hver vej. Overlappet gør hele øverste række og midten blå, mens de øvrige nåede pladser bliver røde.
da.Overlay both drawings. Treat each straig: Læg de to tegninger oven på hinanden. Hvert lige stykke mellem to naboprikker er et snorestykke. Når et stykke fra den ene tegning krydser et fra den anden mellem prikkerne, fjernes begge. Møder ved en prik bevares.
da.Remove the diagonal segments cut between: Fjern de diagonale stykker, der klippes mellem prikkerne. Resten danner en øvre og en nedre forgrening med lodrette stammer samt to korte, adskilte diagonaler nær de øverste hjørner.
da.Slide and sort the pieces by size: Skub og sortér brikkerne efter størrelse
da.Push all pieces in the arrow’s direction: Skub alle brikker i pilens retning. Små brikker passerer store og når de yderste ledige pladser først. Højde og lodret placering bevares. Brikker kan dele kolonne uden lodret overlap. Lige høje brikker bevarer deres indbyrdes vandrette rækkefølge.
da.The arrow points right. Fit the shortest: Pilen peger mod højre. Placér først de korteste brikker længst til højre, så brikkerne på to felter og derefter de højere brikker til venstre for dem. Ingen brik flytter op eller ned eller ændrer størrelse.
da.All black dividers simultaneously move o: Alle sorte streger flytter samtidig én plads mod højre, hvis den næste plads indeholder en gul kugle. En streg med en anden streg foran sig venter. Højre kant fortsætter ved venstre kant.
da.Apply one simultaneous step to the middl: Flyt én gang ud fra midterbilledets placeringer. Den sidste rækkefølge bliver streg, kugle, streg, kugle, streg, streg, kugle.
da.Expand the colours and keep the largest: Udvid farverne og bevar den største gruppe
da.Replace every coloured ball with four ne: Erstat hver farvet kugle med fire nye i samme farve: én oppe, nede, til venstre og til højre. Kugler uden for gitteret forsvinder. På hver plads bevares den farve, flest kugler ankommer i. Ved lighed mellem de største grupper bliver pladsen tom.
